hypotheses.text: Cycle 1 (B65 review, 101 probes reproduced): the misses come from listing phrasings instead of reading structures. Hypothesis: (a) a whitelist for what is attached to the title's remote label (geography, time zone, contract type, travel), (b) a negator within four vetted words of a remote word in either direction, (c) presence read as a frequency, weekday range or day count next to a capitalised place or a workplace, prefixed compounds, owner-less client sites and the travel exemption limited to occasional travel, and (d) hiding tiers also reading an NFKC, zero-width-free copy of the text together hide all 101 review probes, keep every table row, move no stored posting toward showing and cost at most 6 of the 102 catalog postings; plus a bounded owner token (no quadratic time) and a rollback that checks each row's digest before writing.

Cycle 2 (re-review of cycle 1): (a) the title check keys on REMOTE_TITLE's exact label shape, so '- Remote (Austin campus)', 'Remote US, Austin studio' or '(Remote; Austin campus)' skip it: reading every standalone 'remote' word in the title (skipping the job name after a leading one) closes H1; (b) TITLE_WORDS backtracks quadratically because a lazy core meets a repeated optional suffix: capping titles at 300 characters and stripping affixes with anchored single passes makes titles linear and fixes 'Worldwide'; (c) the remaining negation, presence and office-word misses (H2, H3, M4) and the false exclusions of common remote wording (M3) are vocabulary edges of the same structures. Testable: every re-review probe hidden, the M3 controls not excluded, a 99,000-character title under 100 ms, no stored posting moves toward showing, catalog cost at most 8 of 102.
